title: Hazily Steamed Russian Barramundi Pilaf
description: A buttery, pillowy, nostalgic Russian dish featuring barramundi and a steaming copper pot. This recipe is designed to be Buddhist-temple-friendly, using brine-dried barramundi for a delightful twist.
instructions: Rinse the coarse rice in a fine-mesh strainer and drain well.
Combine the water and coarse rice in a heatproof bowl and let soak for 30 minutes.
Rinse the brine-dried barramundi fillet under cold water, pat dry with paper towels, and slice into 1-inch pieces.
In a copper steaming pot, melt the unsalted butter over medium heat.
Add the dill weed and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the coarse rice to the copper steaming pot and stir to combine with the butter and dill weed.
Add the brine-dried barramundi pieces to the copper steaming pot and stir to combine with the rice and butter.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Pour the soaked rice and water mixture into the copper steaming pot and stir to combine.
Cover the copper steaming pot and steam over boiling water for 18-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Fluff the pilaf with a fork and stir in the chopped scallions and sour cream.
Serve immediately, garnished with additional scallions and dill weed if desired.
